venue.name: YMCA / YWCA of Vancouver Island Camp Thunderbird
venue.description: The Y Outdoor Centre, home of Camp Thunderbird, sits in the Sooke Hills on 1200 acres of forest beside a 7 acre lake, and has run outdoor experiences for children and youth since 1935. It offers day and one to four night outdoor education visits for school classes, community groups such as scouts, and home schoolers, with programming, meals and accommodation all included. Programs are aligned to the BC curriculum for K to 12 learners and run in May and June. The camp also rents its buildings and cabins to groups, and sends staff out to run teambuilding sessions in the Greater Victoria area.
venue.address: 5040 Glinz Lake Road, Sooke, BC V9Z 0E3

facility_notes.washrooms: The three Animal Cabins have a 3-piece washroom in cabin. The yurts have a shower and washroom house nearby, and the Shrub Cabins have a shower house and outhouse nearby.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Day groups can choose to eat in the dining hall or bring their own lunches, which are enjoyed in a picnic area at camp.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Coach buses do not fit on Camp Thunderbird roads. Only school buses should be booked for student transportation. If this poses a barrier, please contact us.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: We can arrange for additional supports such as all-terrain wheelchair rental. Please contact us to discuss how we might work together.

restrictions: We ask that peanut and nut products are not brought to Camp Thunderbird.
Coach buses do not fit on Camp Thunderbird roads. Only school buses should be booked for student transportation.
One of the accompanying adults must be a certified first aid attendant.
A vehicle must be brought to the site and must be available and designated as the emergency vehicle.
Children under the age of 12 must be directly supervised at all times.
Chaperones are required to sleep in the cabins with the campers to provide support and supervision.
We request that students not bring electronics to camp.
No food is kept in the cabins.
Our kitchen/cooking facilities are not available for group use. All food prepared in our commercial kitchen must be prepared by our kitchen staff.
The Y Outdoor Centre / Camp Thunderbird is a non-smoking and non-vaping facility.
venue.seasonal_notes: Curriculum-aligned Outdoor Education programs are available in May and June.

programs.name: Day Outdoor Education Program
programs.description: A full day at Camp Thunderbird run by camp instructors. Teachers arrange students into activity groups of 10 to 14, and each group rotates through three or four sessions chosen with the camp, from canoeing, kayaking, stand up paddleboarding, rock climbing, archery, orienteering, hiking, teambuilding, low ropes, campcraft, owl pellet dissection and nature walks. Arrival is 9:00am and departure is 4:00pm. You either bring your own lunch or pay more to eat in the dining hall. New for 2026 there is an extended day option running 9am to 7:30pm that adds dinner and an evening campfire. Swimming is not offered to day groups because of the time the swim challenge takes. French programming is available for groups of up to 55 participants.
programs.what_children_do: Children spend the whole day outdoors in a small group with a camp instructor, moving between three or four activities. They paddle a canoe or kayak on Glinz Lake, shoot on an outdoor archery range, work through teambuilding challenges and walk forest trails. They eat lunch in the dining hall or at a picnic area outside, then finish the afternoon with a big group game such as Capture the Flag.
programs.our_note: This is a real day outdoors, not a tour, so children need closed toed shoes, rain gear and a full change of clothes. Your group has to supply one adult per activity group, a certified first aid attendant and a vehicle to act as the emergency car. The prices on their fees page are from 2017, so ask for a current quote when you enquire.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms, a dining hall and indoor halls are on site, and lunch is either yours to bring or theirs to provide for more. Rain arrangements are not published and the price is years out of date, so both are worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $46.00 rate is for bringing your own lunch. Lunch provided in the dining hall is $56.00 per participant. Additional fees may apply if arriving or departing at non-standard times.
programs.payment_timing: Deposit of $500 or 20% of booking cost, whichever is greater, is due within 30 days of contract date. A final invoice is sent after your visit.
programs.cancellation_note: With over 90 days notice the initial payment is returned less a $100 administration fee. With 60 to 90 days notice the initial payment is forfeited. With less than 60 days notice you are billed for 90% of the total booking cost. Cancellations must be submitted in writing.
programs.evidence: Fees assume a minimum of 13 participants. Arrival is 9:00am and departure is 4:00pm

programs.name: Overnight Outdoor Education Program
programs.description: A one to four night stay at Camp Thunderbird with programming, meals and accommodation all included. Arrival is 10:00am and departure is 2:00pm on the last day. Students are arranged into activity groups of 10 to 14 and rotate through activities such as canoeing, kayaking, rock climbing on natural rock, archery, orienteering, hiking, atlatl, low ropes, campcraft and teambuilding, with evening wide games and campfires. Swimming is only offered to groups staying overnight because of the time the swim challenge takes. Chaperones sleep in the cabins with the students. Grade 7 groups can add the Climate Alive and Natural Selection science programs. Their most popular stay is 2 nights.
programs.what_children_do: Children sleep in bunk beds in a cabin or yurt with an adult from their own group, and eat family style at tables of up to ten in the dining hall. Across the days they paddle on Glinz Lake, climb real rock, shoot archery, navigate an orienteering course and walk forest trails. Evenings are wide games like Capture the Flag, then skits and songs around a campfire.
programs.our_note: Chaperones sleep in the cabins and supervise before and after every meal, so you need one adult for every eight children and they need to be up for it. Cell reception is patchy and children are asked to leave phones at home, which is the point but worth warning families about. The published fees are from 2017, so ask for a current quote.
programs.practical_summary: Beds, all meals, washrooms and shower houses are on site, and one adult per eight children comes at no charge. Your group has to bring a certified first aid attendant and a vehicle to use as the emergency car.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $134.00 rate is for one night and four meals. Two nights and seven meals is $212.00, three nights and ten meals is $288.00, and four nights and thirteen meals is $357.00, all per participant. Additional cabins, if available, cost $100 to $200 per night depending on the type of cabin.
programs.payment_timing: Deposit of $1000 or 20% of booking cost, whichever is greater, is due within 30 days of contract date. A final invoice is sent after your visit and payment by credit card is capped at $5,000.
programs.cancellation_note: With over 90 days notice the initial payment is returned less a $100 administration fee. With 60 to 90 days notice the initial payment is forfeited. With less than 60 days notice you are billed for 90% of the total booking cost. Cancellations must be submitted in writing.
programs.evidence: Fees assume a minimum of 20 people unless there are multiple groups on-site at once.

programs.name: Mobile Teambuilding (camp staff come to you)
programs.description: Camp Thunderbird staff travel to your school or community centre anywhere in the Greater Victoria area and run a teambuilding session there. The fee covers program planning, staff and all props and materials. Sessions run for three, four, five or six hours, and the published fees cover groups of up to 60 participants.
programs.what_children_do: Children stay at their own school or centre and work through group games and challenges led by camp instructors, starting with simple tasks and building to harder ones that only work if the whole group co-operates.
programs.our_note: This is the option when a bus out to Sooke is not realistic. The published price is for the whole group rather than for each child, so a full class spreads it further than a small one. Ask what indoor and outdoor space they need before you commit.
programs.practical_summary: Everything is brought to you, including staff, planning and equipment. Ages, months and the space required are not published, so ask about all three when you enquire.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $606.00 rate is a three hour session for 30 participants or fewer. Four hours is $755.00, five hours is $881.00 and six hours is $967.00 at that size. For 31 to 60 participants, three hours is $1209.00, four hours is $1508.00, five hours is $1751.00 and six hours is $1942.00.
programs.payment_timing: Deposit of $500 or 20% of booking cost, whichever is greater, is due within 30 days of contract date.
programs.evidence: Staff will come to your school or community centre within the Greater Victoria Area. Fees include program planning, staff, props/materials.

programs.name: Camp Site and Building Rental
programs.description: You can rent Camp Thunderbird and run your own programme. Overnight rental fees include a group liaison and use of the buildings, cabins and meeting spaces, charged at $33.00 a bed and $11.50 a meal. Day rental groups pay a use fee for the building they use, either Shoemaker Hall for up to 50 people or Hyas House for up to 200. Camp staff can lead activities such as rock climbing, high ropes, boating on the lake, archery, orienteering and an evening wide game with campfire, each charged separately and subject to availability. All food prepared in the commercial kitchen must be prepared by camp kitchen staff. Standard check in is 3:00pm, check out from cabins is 8:00am and site departure is 2:00pm. The camp is alcohol and tobacco free and does not rent for weddings or parties.
programs.our_note: This is the do it yourself option. You get the buildings, the beds and the meals, and you run the programme yourself. If you want camp staff to lead climbing or boating, book that early because it is charged separately and depends on availability.
programs.practical_summary: Cabins, yurts, a dining hall and an indoor hall are on site, with shower houses and washrooms nearby. Bookings assume at least 20 people and overnight groups get priority, so a small day group may struggle to get a date.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $361.00 rate is a day trip using Shoemaker Hall, which holds 50. A day trip using Hyas House, which holds 200, is $828.00. Overnight rentals are charged $33.00 a bed and $11.50 a meal instead. Staff led activities are extra, for example boating on the lake is $260.00 for up to 14 people for 3 hours.
programs.payment_timing: Deposit of $1000 or 20% of booking cost, whichever is greater, for overnight groups, and $500 for day groups, is due within 30 days of contract date.
programs.evidence: Bookings assume a minimum group size of 20. Priority is given to overnight rental groups.

gaps: PRICE: every fee on the costs page is headed Education Fees 2017 and the linked schedule is OE-Fees-2017.pdf, so all prices in this record are nine years old. Ask for a current quote.

PRICE: the Mobile Teambuilding table is headed as a fee for each participant but its rows are banded by group size, so it reads as a fee for the whole group. Recorded as a group fee. See the recorded disagreement.

AGE: no youngest age is published anywhere. Programs are described as aligned to the BC curriculum for K to 12 learners, and there is no statement about under fives, so a daycare group should ask directly.
AGE: the Mobile Teambuilding session has no published age or grade range at all.

CAPACITY: no maximum group size is published for the day or overnight outdoor education programs. The activity group table runs up to 140 participants with 10 camp staff, but that is not stated as a limit.
LEAD TIME: no minimum notice is published. Booking requests received by October 15 at 5pm are balanced for the following season, but they also say they take bookings close to the start of the season.
RAIN BACKUP: not stated. There is indoor program space in Shoemaker Hall and a dining hall, and the gear list assumes rain, but there is no published wet weather policy.

ACCESSIBILITY: no step free or stroller information is published. The booklet offers to arrange an all terrain wheelchair rental, which is a support offer rather than a statement that the site is accessible.
MONTHS: the outdoor education season is stated as May and June. No months are published for site rentals or for Mobile Teambuilding.
The camp phone number is given three different ways across their own pages. See the recorded disagreement.
The outdoor education contact email is spelled with two different endings across their own pages. See the recorded disagreement.

Individually registered summer camps, both day and overnight, also run at this site for grades 1 to 10, but a parent signs up one child at a time, so they are not a bookable group visit and are not recorded here.

IMAGES: the two photographs on the outdoor education overview page carousel are only served at 300 by 200 pixels, which is too small to use, so they were skipped. Neither photograph recorded here carries alt text on the site, so both alt lines were written after opening the images in a browser and looking at them.

This is one of three separate records for the YMCA-YWCA of Vancouver Island. The other two, the Downtown Y in Victoria and the Westhills Y in Langford, are membership recreation centres that publish no group visit. All of the organisation's school and group outdoor education runs here at Camp Thunderbird.
LOCATION: the camp publishes a street address but no map with coordinates, so the pin still needs to be geocoded from the address.

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different answers for how many adults have to come on an overnight stay. One says one adult per nine children, the other says one per eight. We use one per eight, from their 2026 teacher booklet. Worth settling when you book, because it changes how many staff you need.

conflicts.note: The price for bringing camp staff to your school is confusing on their own page. The column is labelled as a price for each participant, but the rows are priced by group size, so it reads as a price for the whole group. We have taken it as the whole group. Confirm the total before you commit.

Three different phone numbers for the camp appear across their pages. We use the one their camp page calls the new number. If it does not connect, the older camp line and the main Y office number are both still listed.
The same camp address is written two ways on their own pages, one ending in ca and one in com. We use the ca version, which is what the rest of their site uses. If one bounces, try the other.
